extracted.intended_audience: readers of Rabelais / scholars of satire and classical divination lore
extracted.subtask_description: An excerpt from Rabelais' Gargantua & Pantagruel that discusses how to consult oracles and how to interpret prophetic signs (verbal, written, and gestural), with examples (dumb prophets, sneezes, numeric gestures, dying poets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer signs/gestures over written or spoken oracles
rubrics_metrics.description: The surest and most veritable oracles were not those which either were delivered in writing or uttered by word of mouth in speaking. Those which were represented then by signs and outward gestures were accounted the truest and the most infallible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rabelais (via Pantagruel) argues that verbal or brief written prophecies are often ambiguous (amphibologies, equivocations). Gestural or sign-based divination reduces equivocity. Anti-pattern: trusting short, cryptic written verses without considering nonverbal corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a deaf‑from‑birth (congenitally deaf) mute as prophet
rubrics_metrics.description: It were requisite that the dumb you consult with be such as have been deaf from the hour of their nativity, and consequently dumb; for none can be so lively, natural, and kindly dumb as he who never heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: gestures of a congenital mute are presented as more 'natural' and not secondarily learned from spoken language, so their signs are less likely to be adulterated by imitation. Anti-pattern: using someone who only became mute later (their gestures may echo learned speech patterns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer authentic, un‑affected gestures (avoid affectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: To the end that his gestures and signs may be the more vively and truly prophetic, and not counterfeit by the intermixture of some adulterate lustre and affectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose gesturers whose signs are natural and not theatrical/artificial. Example: Pantagruel warns against counterfeit or affected gesticulation. Anti-pattern: relying on ostentatious performers whose gestures are rehearsed or affected, which may mislead interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware interpreter bias (gendered/sexualized readings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The greater part of women... do always represent unto their fancies, think, and imagine, that it hath some relation to the sugared entering of the goodly ithyphallos... they will interpret the whole in reference to the act of androgynation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for the interpreter's predispositions: some readers (here, many women, in Panurge's caricature) may sexualize or otherwise bias the meaning of signs. Anti-pattern: uncritically accepting a single interpreter's sexualized or culturally bounded reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeric and emblematic hand‑signs carry specific symbolic meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: He made the figure of the Greek letter Tau... it denotes marriage, and withal the number thirty... he stretched out all the five fingers... Pythagoras called five the nuptial number, which, together with marriage, signifieth the consummation of matrimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret hand gestures with attention to established symbolic systems (Pythagorean numerology, cultural customs such as lighting five wedding tapers). Examples: tau = marriage/30; five fingers = nuptial number. Anti-pattern: ignoring culturally specific numeric symbolism and treating gestures as arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction of bodily signs (e.g., sneezing) can be read as omens
rubrics_metrics.description: This sneezing... if done towards the right side, it imports... lucky, good, and happy. The quite contrary thereto is thereby implied and presaged if it be done towards the left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small bodily phenomena (such as sneezing) are given prognostic value; note direction and context. Source cited: doctrine of Terpsion. Anti-pattern: treating such signs as meaningless without reference to the tradition that assigns them significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dying poets and elders often become prophetic
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets... when they are drawing near their latter end do ordinarily become prophets, and by the inspiration of that god sing sweetly in vaticinating things which are to come... old decrepit men upon the brinks of Charon’s banks do usher their decease with a disclosure... of the determinate and assured truth of future accidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek out poets or aged persons near death as potential sources of reliable prophecy (Raminagrobis example). Corollary: swan-song lore (swans sing before dying) is invoked as an analogy. Anti-pattern: dismissing late-life utterances as incoherent without considering prophetic tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written or brief prophecies are prone to ambiguity (amphibology)
rubrics_metrics.description: In their interpretation, right witty, learned, and ingenious men have been deceived through amphibologies, equivoques, and obscurity of words, no less than by the brevity of their sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat short or cryptic verbal/written prophecies with caution; look for fuller contexts or corroborating signs. Anti-pattern: literalizing brief verses without exploring multiple readings or consulting other modes (gestures, dying utterances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor allegorical/multiple readings over crude literalism
rubrics_metrics.description: You interpret this to theft and larceny... I love the exposition, and the allegory pleaseth me; but not according to the sense whereto you stretch it... That a marvellously fearful thing is love, and that true love is never without fear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When prophetic phrases are coarse or obscene in literal reading (e.g., sexual language), consider allegorical or temperate interpretations (psychological, social, symbolic). Anti-pattern: insisting on pornographic or base literal senses when allegorical readings better fit context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatrical gesticulators can function as cross‑linguistic interpreters
rubrics_metrics.description: With this man alone, sufficient for supplying all their places, will that great inconveniency hereafter be totally removed; seeing he is such a fine gesticulator... that with his very fingers he doth speak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A skilled stage performer (Jack‑pudding) may communicate effectively across language barriers by expressive gesture; such performers can be enlisted where interpreters are scarce. Anti-pattern: assuming gestures are universally understood without considering performer's skill or cultural conventions.
